solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Italian probes AAA giant PLCs hit by revenue charge

indicators.note: something that probes pokes inside, so these letters go into the middle of the others
the letters are knocked about by the blow, so they are rearranged

parts.note: X stands for 'by' as in measurements, 3 by 4 written 3x4

explanation.surface: A financial report: an Italian investigator looks into huge top-rated companies squeezed by the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' scrambles AAA GIANT PLCS, which 'probes' says IT goes into; the X for 'by' closes it. 'Revenue' looks like part of the wordplay but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital gains tax is a levy the revenue authorities charge on profit from selling assets.

clue.text: Which might show live celebs at No1 behaving badly?

definitions.text: Which might show live celebs at No1 behaving badly?

indicators.note: letters that behave badly will not stay in their places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: No is taken as written and the figure 1 stands for the letter I

explanation.surface: A television channel that broadcasts badly behaved celebrities at number one.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 reads as the letter I, so the fodder is LIVECELEBSATNOI, fifteen letters, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmes delivered by wire into homes can certainly broadcast misbehaving stars live.

clue.text: Runs into couple that is plain

indicators.note: the runs letter is put into the word for couple

parts.note: a couple is a pair
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a couple out on open flat ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide, flat, treeless grassland, a plain in the noun sense.

clue.text: Gain courage from the karate chop?

indicators.note: a chop breaks the words up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking confidence from a well-landed martial arts blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'karate chop' reads as one thing, but 'chop' is the anagram signal working on THE KARATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heart is an idiom for becoming encouraged or regaining confidence.

clue.text: Solitary character extended golf breaks

indicators.note: golf breaks away, leaving the word without that letter

parts.note: something extended is made longer
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lone figure stretches out a round of golf, taking breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is a person who prefers to be alone, a solitary sort.

clue.text: Rated dad getting up changing diapers

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: the letters of diapers are changed around

explanation.surface: A father is judged on getting up to change the baby's nappies.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess or value something, so appraised means evaluated.

clue.text: Spanish chap cycling from Scandinavia?

indicators.note: letters cycle round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: señor is the Spanish for a man or gentleman

explanation.surface: A Spaniard pedals in from northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the first two letters of SENOR to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes the people and language of medieval Norway and wider Scandinavia.

clue.text: Listening to radio song — terrible noise!

parts.note: a song is a tune
a din is a loud, unpleasant noise

explanation.surface: A complaint about a song heard on the radio: what a racket!
explanation.definitionFit: Being tuned in means having a receiver set to a station and following its broadcast.

clue.text: They hang around the house until early January

definitions.text: They hang around the house until early January

parts.words: They hang around the house until early January
parts.note: sounds like idle loiterers, but means festive adornments that come down by Twelfth Night

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang around' suggests lingering guests; the tradition is to take festive trimmings down by Twelfth Night, 5 or 6 January.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel, baubles and paper chains are put up for the festive season and removed in early January.

clue.text: Defame Fern after changing sides

indicators.note: the letter for right is swapped for the letter for left

parts.note: bracken is a common fern

explanation.surface: Slandering a plant after defecting to the other party.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are right and left, so changing sides swaps R for L.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken someone's name is to damage their reputation by slander.

clue.text: Stop Iran harbour catching fish

indicators.note: the phrase catches the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: A naval call to stop Iran's port from fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a South American freshwater fish famed for sharp teeth.

clue.text: Planet core hot to the east

indicators.note: in an across clue east is the right-hand end, so the letter shifts there

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A planet whose hot core lies towards the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, our home world.

clue.text: A red deer going out around noon hit from behind by a car

definitions.text: hit from behind by a car

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the letter for noon
the letters go out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deer wandering out at midday is struck from behind by a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be rear-ended is to be struck at the back by another vehicle.

clue.text: Look carefully at opener for Lord's Test series — they might bat

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it closely

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter

parts.note: the Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia

explanation.surface: Watching the opening batsman at Lord's in an Ashes match.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground. 'Bat' looks like cricket but means blink.
explanation.definitionFit: To bat one's eyelashes is to flutter them, so the fringe of hair on the lids does the batting.

clue.text: Hay animal chewed is from the highest mountains

indicators.note: chewed food is broken up and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grazing beast munching hay up in the high peaks, like a yak.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayas contain Everest and the world's other tallest peaks, so Himalayan describes things from there.

clue.text: Pessimist starts to cancel yearly National Insurance contributions

indicators.note: the starts of the following words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A gloomy person begins cancelling annual National Insurance payments.
explanation.walkthrough: National Insurance is the UK's compulsory social security contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic expects the worst of people's motives, a doubting and gloomy outlook.

clue.text: Caught up-to-date broadcast — it's a revolution!

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Catching up on the latest news bulletin about an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is a sudden seizure of government power, an overthrow.

clue.text: Brilliance of chapter in revolutionary tale

indicators.note: the chapter letter is placed in the turned-round word
something revolutionary turns over, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Praising a dazzling chapter in a story of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Tale backwards is ELAT, with C put in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is a striking success or showy brilliance of performance.

clue.text: Secular Tory is boring, terse, to the point

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so the Tory goes inside

parts.note: laic means lay, non-clerical, secular
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A political sketch: a non-religious Conservative is dull and brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, concise and brief.

clue.text: Halfway through some basic maths, by the sea in France when it's hot?

parts.note: mid means in the middle of
a sum is a simple arithmetic problem
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A schoolchild doing sums at a French seaside resort in the summer heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer falls in late June, the height of the summer season, normally a warm time.

clue.text: Scottish King introducing an honour to American subject

indicators.note: the honour is introduced into the middle of the subject

parts.note: Americans call mathematics math
the CBE, Commander of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch bringing a British honour to a US citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American subject' suggests a US citizen, but it is the school subject spelt the American way.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth was an 11th-century King of Scots, made famous by Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Like orbiting fashionable society groups?

parts.note: in means trendy, in fashion
circles are social groups, as in literary circles

explanation.surface: Asking whether trendy social sets are like things going round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbiting bodies travel round and round, moving in loops.

clue.text: Carry off old time machine

parts.note: to carry off goods unlawfully is to rob

explanation.surface: Stealing an old time machine, as in science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automated mechanical device that performs tasks.

clue.text: Rascal removing tail from Dublin Bay prawns

indicators.note: the tail is the last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: scampi are Dublin Bay prawns, also called langoustines

explanation.surface: A rogue peeling the tails off shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing a prawn's tail is literal kitchen work, but here it means dropping the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous person, a naughty youngster.

clue.text: Tube accepts American money

indicators.note: the tube takes the American letter inside it

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: The London Underground now takes US dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground but is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold coin used across Europe, hence a crossword word for cash.

clue.text: Lobbying corruptly to have a bishop sacked in an ungentlemanly way

indicators.note: corrupt letters are spoiled from their proper order, so rearranged
the bishop is sacked, so that letter goes from the pool

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is dismissed for corrupt lobbying, a dishonourable affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignobly means dishonourably, lacking the noble conduct expected of a gentleman.

clue.text: Educator sadly leaves university design movement

indicators.note: letters treated sadly are put out of order, so rearranged
the university letter leaves the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A teacher departs the university, regretfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco was a 1920s and 1930s style of architecture and decorative arts.

clue.text: With which those hoping to kick the habit get plastered?

definitions.text: With which those hoping to kick the habit get plastered?

parts.words: With which those hoping to kick the habit get plastered?
parts.note: plastered suggests drunk, but means wearing a stick-on dressing that releases a drug

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' would usually mean drunk; here it means covered with a sticking plaster delivering the drug through the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers trying to quit wear adhesive skin pads that release a dose of the addictive drug.
